rows: Deck Scene of the Great Eastern

Robert Howlett photographed the deck of the Great Eastern, the biggest ship in the world, while it was being built in 1857. Workers stand on the huge iron deck, and the picture makes the giant ship seem like a floating town.
How many people can you see on the deck?
Courtyard of the Alhambra
Charles Clifford photographed the Court of the Lions in the Alhambra palace in Granada, Spain, with a lone man sitting on a step. The man gives the picture a sense of scale and calm.
How does the man make the courtyard look bigger?
Temple of Maharraqa, Nubia
Francis Frith photographed a small temple in Nubia, in southern Egypt, in 1857. Frith traveled up the Nile three times with a huge camera, and his photographs were bestsellers in Britain.
Why might travelers want pictures of faraway temples?
Church of the Ascension, Jerusalem
Francis Frith photographed the Church of the Ascension on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem in 1857. His pictures of the Holy Land were popular with people who could not travel.
Why would people want to see the Holy Land?
North Shore of the Dead Sea
Francis Frith photographed the barren shore of the Dead Sea in 1857. The water is so salty that people float on it, and Frith's picture shows the empty, bright landscape.
Why do people float easily in very salty water?
Alfred Tennyson by Lewis Carroll
Lewis Carroll, the author of Alice in Wonderland, photographed the poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson in 1857. Carroll was a keen amateur photographer who made portraits of famous people and of children.
What would you say to a famous poet?
Avenue of the Banyan Trees, Srirangam
Linnaeus Tripe photographed a road lined with banyan trees at Srirangam in southern India in 1858. The trees arch over like a green tunnel.
What is it like to walk under old trees?
Taj Mahal, Back View of the Rest-House
Dr. John Murray photographed the Taj Mahal and the rest-house behind it, with a person for scale. Murray was a doctor who loved to photograph India's historic buildings.
Why would a doctor take up photography?
Chutter Manzil Palace, Lucknow
Felice Beato photographed the Chattar Manzil, a palace in Lucknow, India, in 1858, with the king's boat shaped like a fish moored near it. Beato recorded the city soon after a long siege.
What shape is the king's boat?
Tomb of Saadat Ali, Kaiserbagh Palace
Felice Beato photographed the tomb of Saadat Ali Khan in the Kaiserbagh Palace in Lucknow. The domed buildings stand in the middle of the city.
How many domes can you see?
The Residency, Seen from the Redan Battery
Felice Beato photographed the ruined Residency at Lucknow, where British people were besieged in 1857. The pitted walls show the shelling.
What do the broken walls tell you?
Asaf-ud-Daula's Imambara
Beato photographed the Bara Imambara in Lucknow, a huge shrine built by Asaf-ud-Daula in the 1780s with a giant arched hall. It is one of the biggest rooms with no pillars in the world.
How do you make a giant room without pillars?
La Martinière School, Lucknow
Beato photographed La Martinière, a school in Lucknow built by the French soldier Claude Martin in the 1790s. It looks like a palace with towers and statues.
Why would a school look like a palace?
Nayak Darbar Hall, Thanjavur
Linnaeus Tripe photographed the Nayak Darbar Hall in the palace of Thanjavur in southern India in 1858. His photographs of Indian buildings were published in a series.
What do the arches and columns look like?
Entrance to the Port of Brest
Gustave Le Gray photographed the entrance to Brest harbor in France in 1858. Le Gray often photographed harbors and the sea, where the sky and water are both sharp.
What kind of ships would use a harbor like this?
Julia Jackson
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed her niece Julia Jackson in 1859. Julia later became the mother of the writer Virginia Woolf.
What is soft about the picture?
Rustic Bridge, Sleepy Hollow
William England photographed a rustic bridge in Sleepy Hollow, New York, the home of Washington Irving's ghost story. He took stereographs in America in 1859.
What spooky story might have happened here?
Canadian Locomotive Spitfire
William England photographed the locomotive Spitfire of the Canadian Grand Trunk Railway in 1859. He photographed new technology such as engines and bridges.
What does a steam locomotive need to run?
The Capitol Under Construction
William England photographed the U.S. Capitol dome while it was being built in 1859. The dome was rising above the old building, and cranes and scaffolding fill the view.
Why would a photographer record a building under construction?
Along the Tops, Roof of Victoria Bridge, Montreal
William England photographed the roof of the Victoria Bridge in Montreal, then the longest bridge in the world. Workers walk along the iron roof high above the river.
Would you walk along the roof of a bridge?
Temple of Ramesses II, Abu Simbel
Antonio Beato photographed the great temple of Abu Simbel in Egypt, where giant statues of Ramesses II sat covered in sand. Prints of the temple were sold to travelers on the Nile.
Why did the sand cover the statues?
Yosemite Valley from the Mariposa Trail
Charles Leander Weed made some of the first photographs of Yosemite Valley in 1859 and 1860. This view from the Mariposa Trail shows the valley as visitors first saw it.
What do you think visitors felt at their first sight?
The Schreckhorn, Grindelwald
Francis Frith photographed the Schreckhorn, a high peak in the Swiss Alps, in the 1860s. The name means the Peak of Terror.
Why would a mountain be named the Peak of Terror?
Mer de Glace, Chamonix
Francis Frith photographed the Mer de Glace, a huge river of ice in the French Alps, in the 1860s. The name means Sea of Ice, and you can see the cracks and ridges.
What does a glacier do over time?
Bull Run
Timothy O'Sullivan and Andrew J. Russell photographed the stream and ruins at Bull Run, Virginia, in 1862. The creek ran through the first big battlefield of the Civil War.
What does a battlefield look like months later?
Military Bridge Across the Chickahominy
David B. Woodbury photographed an army bridge across the Chickahominy River in Virginia in 1862. Engineers built bridges quickly to move armies across swamps.
How could soldiers build a bridge so fast?
Francis Wayland Sherman at Age Two
A small boy named Francis Wayland Sherman, age 2 years 10 months, posed for a portrait in 1862. The inscription on the back of the photograph records his age to the month.
Why would a parent write the age to the month?
Stone Bridge at Bull Run
George Barnard photographed the ruined stone bridge at Bull Run in 1862 looking upstream. He photographed battlefields and railroads for the Union army.
Why was the bridge ruined?
Burnside's Bridge, Antietam
Alexander Gardner photographed the stone bridge at Antietam, Maryland, where Union General Burnside's men crossed the creek under fire in September 1862. It is still called Burnside's Bridge.
Why would a bridge be hard to cross in a battle?
Photographers Resting in Camp
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed fellow photographers resting in a camp in Virginia. It is a rare look at the people who made the Civil War pictures, along with their wagon darkroom.
How would you carry a darkroom on a wagon?
Bullock Cart, Delhi
A bullock cart pulled by two oxen carries goods through Delhi in 1863. The picture records transport that had been used for thousands of years.
How fast does an ox cart go?
Shimla: Houses of European Residents
Samuel Bourne photographed houses of British residents in the hill town of Shimla, India, in 1863. The town was the summer capital of British India.
Why did the officials move to the hills in summer?
Delhi: The Emperor's Palace, Hall of Private Audience
Samuel Bourne photographed the Diwan-i-Khas, the Hall of Private Audience in the Red Fort in Delhi. The marble hall once held the Peacock Throne.
What would you want to say to an emperor in this room?
Delhi: The Jama Masjid
Bourne photographed the north side of the Jama Masjid, the great mosque of Delhi. It is among the largest mosques in India.
How many domes can you count?
Delhi: The Qutub Minar
Bourne photographed the Qutub Minar, a tall tower of red sandstone in Delhi, built in the 1200s. It is 72 meters high.
How tall do you think this tower is?
Delhi: Great Arch and Iron Pillar near the Qutub Minar
Bourne photographed an ancient iron pillar that has not rusted in 1,600 years. It stands in the Qutub complex in Delhi.
Why do you think iron doesn't rust there?
Nadar, Self-Portrait in Indian Costume
Nadar loved to dress up in costumes for the camera. Around 1863 he made a self-portrait in a headdress and a costume he called Indian.
Why did people dress up for photographs?
George MacDonald
Lewis Carroll photographed the Scottish writer George MacDonald in 1863. MacDonald wrote fairy tales and encouraged Carroll to publish Alice in Wonderland.
Why would one author encourage another?
Alfred Waud at Gettysburg
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed Alfred Waud, a newspaper artist for Harper's Weekly, sketching a scene at Gettysburg in 1863. Waud drew the war for readers at home.
How did newspapers show war before photographs could be printed?
Field Where General Reynolds Fell, Gettysburg
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed the woods where Union General John Reynolds was killed on the first day of the Battle of Gettysburg. The peaceful field makes the loss feel sad.
How can a calm place be sad?
Charles Hay Cameron
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed her husband, Charles Hay Cameron, a lawyer and scholar, in 1864. He had a long white beard that photographers loved.
Why would a photographer love a white beard?
Paris Sewers, Boat
Nadar photographed the Paris sewers by electric light in 1864. A boat is carried through the tunnels, which were a new wonder of the underground city.
Why would someone photograph a sewer?
Grant's Council of War
General Ulysses S. Grant smokes a cigar with his back to the camera while officers talk at a council of war, 1864. It is a casual and famous scene from the late Civil War.
How can you tell who is in charge?
White House Landing, Pamunkey River
This study shows river steamers and barges tied up at a Union supply base in Virginia in 1864. The base shipped food and ammunition to Grant's army.
Why would an army need so many boats?
Atlanta Railroad Depot
George Barnard photographed the railroad depot in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1864 after Sherman's army took the city. Atlanta was a rail hub, and its depot was crucial.
Why does a city need a railroad station?
Sherman's Men Destroying Railroad
Union soldiers twist railroad rails by heating them over burning wooden ties, then bending them around trees. These twisted rails were called Sherman's neckties.
Why would soldiers wreck railroad tracks?
Francis Planté
Nadar photographed the French pianist Francis Planté in 1865. Planté was a famous pianist who played into his nineties.
How do pianists keep their hands strong?
The Dirty Monk
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed the poet Alfred Tennyson in 1865 with long hair and beard, and later called the picture The Dirty Monk. Tennyson said it was his favorite.
Why would the poet call it the Dirty Monk?
The Royal Stag
James Valentine photographed a stag, a male red deer, in the Scottish Highlands in the 1860s. Photographers tried to capture animals, but they moved too much for slow cameras.
How did he keep the stag still?
Twin Babies
The Davis Brothers photographed twin babies in the 1860s. This one has been tinted by hand with color, since color photography was not available until the 20th century.
How do you paint over a photograph?
The Guard House, Colmar
Adolphe Braun photographed the Corps de Garde in Colmar in Alsace, a Renaissance building from 1575. Braun, who came from Alsace, was proud of his town.
What do you notice about the windows?
The Jama Masjid, Delhi
Louis Rousselet photographed the great mosque of Delhi in 1865, hoping to show how splendid India's monuments were. It was built in the 1650s by Emperor Shah Jahan.
Why would a French artist take up photography in India?
Humayun's Tomb, Delhi
Rousselet photographed Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, built in the 1500s, which inspired the Taj Mahal. It is a huge garden tomb of red sandstone and white marble.
How is it like the Taj Mahal?
Qutub Mosque, Delhi
Rousselet photographed the Qutub complex's old mosque, a ruin of arches and carved stone. Some of the stones were reused from earlier temples.
What patterns can you see on the stone arches?
President Andrew Johnson
Mathew Brady's studio made this portrait of Andrew Johnson, the 17th president, in 1865. Johnson became president after Abraham Lincoln was killed, and he was later impeached.
What would it feel like to take over from a famous leader?
Charles Marville's Studio, Boulevard Saint-Jacques
Charles Marville photographed his own studio at 66 Boulevard Saint-Jacques in Paris around 1865. It is a glimpse of the place where a great photographer worked.
Why photograph the place you work?
La Bièvre
Charles Marville photographed the Bièvre, a small river in Paris full of tanneries and mills, around 1865. The river was later covered over and now flows underground.
Why would they cover a river?
